Content: How does the author develop the purpose of Passage `1`?

A.Choice: by describing the life story of an inspiring cook

Key.Rationale: The purpose of this article is to give an overview of the professional life of a famous cook named Fannie Farmer, which the author does by providing details about her career.

B.Choice: by describing how Boston Cooking School began

C.Choice: by describing the history of American cookbooks

D.Choice: by describing how cooking has changed over time

Content: Read this sentence from paragraph `3` of Passage `1`.
:ibox:“While teaching the neighbors’ young daughter to cook, Farmer realized that her instructions to use a ‘pinch’ of this or a ‘lump’ of that were not terribly helpful.”
How do the terms “pinch” and “lump” support the claim that recipes rely on attention to detail?

A.Choice: They prove how rewarding it is to follow cooking recipes.

B.Choice: They suggest that cooks must be trained at cooking schools.

C.Choice: They show that cooks must rush to cook food when using a recipe.

D.Choice: They provide examples of measurements that require cooks to guess.

Key.Rationale: These terms might be hard for a cook to interpret or measure, resulting in a different cooking experience `text(each time)` a person prepares food, which supports the idea in paragraph `1` that some recipes called for guesswork.

Content: Select `bbtext(two)` sentences that are important to include in a summary of Passage `1`.

A.Choice: Fannie Farmer was born on `text(March 23)` in Massachusetts.

B.Choice: Fannie Farmer attended Boston Cooking School at the age of `30`.

C.Choice: Fannie Farmer was `text(one)` of the most important cooks in American history.

Key.Rationale: This is the central idea of the passage and should be added to a summary.

D.Choice: The New York Times wrote an article about the way Fannie Farmer cooked.

E.Choice: The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book was published by Fannie Farmer in the `text(late 1800s)`.

Key.Rationale: This is an important detail that is relevant to the central idea and should be included in a summary of the passage.

Content: Select `bbtext(two)` details from Passage `2` that support the central idea that bread is often overlooked as a food.

A.Choice: “. . . and as a result, from the `text(first)` flat cake has come the perfect loaf.” (paragraph `15`)

B.Choice: “The study of bread making is of no slight importance, and deserves more attention than it receives.” (paragraph `15`)

Key.Rationale: This sentence suggests that not everyone appreciates the value of bread and what goes into baking a good loaf of bread.

C.Choice: “Considering its great value, it seems unnecessary and wrong to find poor bread on the table . . .” (paragraph `16`)

Key.Rationale: This detail suggests that bread is an important food, and as a result, no one should have to eat a poorly made loaf of bread.

D.Choice: “Who does not appreciate the loaf produced by the French baker, who has worked `text(months)` to learn the art of bread making?” (paragraph `16`)

E.Choice: “Bread is made from flour of wheat, or other cereals . . .” (paragraph `17`)

Content: Read this sentence from Passage `2`.

:ibox:“Take pastry flour in the hand; close hand tightly, open, and flour will be in shape, having impression of the lines of the hand, and feeling soft and `ultext(velvety)` to touch.” (paragraph `18`)
What does the word “velvety” in this sentence explain about the flour?

Key.Rationale: The author suggests that flour is like velvet, which means it is smooth and soft.

Content: In Passage `2`, how does the structure of paragraph `18` affect the meaning of the passage?

A.Choice: The chronological structure lists the steps to prepare flour for baking bread.

B.Choice: The cause-and-effect structure demonstrates why baked bread uses yeast to rise.

C.Choice: The compare-and-contrast structure explains which flour to use when baking bread.

Key.Rationale: In this paragraph, the author compares and contrasts the types of flour used for making bread and discusses how to choose the right `text(one)`.

D.Choice: The problem-and-solution structure tells how to bake a loaf of bread from a set of ingredients.

Content: How are Passage `1` and Passage `2` similar?

A.Choice: Both passages come from `text(one)` of Fannie Farmer’s cookbooks.

B.Choice: Both passages describe important events in Fannie Farmer’s career.

C.Choice: Both passages show that Fannie Farmer was passionate about food.

Key.Rationale: `text(Each passage)` contains different information about Fannie Farmer’s interest in food or her fondness for making and serving bread.

D.Choice: Both passages explain how Fannie Farmer prepared food to help people.

Content: Show whether `text(each detail)` is found in Passage `1`, Passage `2`, or both passages.
How does the setting of West Africa add to the plot of the passage?

A.Choice: It shows why Mr. Agbele needs quiet.

B.Choice: It explains why the rooster loves the watch.

C.Choice: It explains why the rooster uses certain words.

Key.Rationale: The setting and Ewe words put the focus on the words the rooster uses, which eventually become his sound.

D.Choice: It shows why Mr. Agbele wants to get up at dawn.

Content: Select `bbtext(two)` ways in which the perspective of Mr. Agbele is developed by the author.

A.Choice: Mr. Agbele convinces the rooster to listen to him, which shows that he is a talented speaker.

B.Choice: Mr. Agbele suggests that the rooster move locations, which shows that he dislikes the other villagers.

C.Choice: Mr. Agbele becomes angry only after he is disturbed many times by the rooster, which shows that he is patient.

Key.Rationale: Mr. Agbele confronts the rooster several times and tries several other methods of staying focused before he loses his temper, showing his patience.

D.Choice: Mr. Agbele refuses to give up when the rooster ignores him, which shows that he wants to always be the winner.

E.Choice: Mr. Agbele spends time studying and finds the rooster distracting, which shows that he is serious about learning.

Key.Rationale: Mr. Agbele likes to study and read, and when the rooster starts crowing all day long, he becomes very distracted and seeks a solution.

Content: Read this excerpt from the passage.
:ibox:“‘I have read that time flies when a person is enjoying himself. Thanks to you, for me time crawls like a worm, like a snail! I am truly at my wits’ end!’” (paragraph `16`)
What effect does the phrase “time crawls like a worm, like a snail” have on the passage?

A.Choice: It stresses how much Mr. Agbele loves the rooster for signaling `text(each hour)`.

B.Choice: It shows that Mr. Agbele thinks that the rooster is a bad friend for ignoring his advice.

C.Choice: It shows that Mr. Agbele wishes that the rooster would help the `text(day)` go by more slowly.

D.Choice: It stresses how upset Mr. Agbele is because the rooster is always interrupting his studying.

Key.Rationale: The figurative language shows that time seems to move slowly for Mr. Agbele lately because the rooster is making him miserable.

Content: Read this excerpt from the passage.
:ibox:“They `ultext(collided)` with an awful confusion of feathers, squawks, and broken branches.” (paragraph `19`)
What does `bbtext(collided)` mean?

Key.Rationale: The rooster crashes into the tree.

Content: How does giving the rooster human features move the plot forward?

A.Choice: The rooster’s talks with Mr. Agbele lead the rooster to do something careless.

Key.Rationale: The personification of the rooster in giving him speech allows him to argue with Mr. Agbele, which leads to the accident, which in turn leads to the rooster’s traditional answer/caw that the story is based around.

B.Choice: The rooster’s cleverness makes Mr. Agbele expect to hear from him all `text(day)` long.

C.Choice: The rooster’s skill to work a watch makes him want to give watches to all the roosters.

D.Choice: The rooster’s decision to help the people in the village leads the rooster to leave his home.

Content: Read this sentence from the passage.
:ibox:“Mr. Agbele became so `ultext(accustomed to)` the question that he hardly heard it.” (paragraph `22`)
What does the phrase `bbtext(accustomed to)` mean as it is used in this sentence?
:ibox:`bbtext(This problem has two parts.)`
What is a theme in the passage?

A.Choice: `text(One)` should always help those in need.

Key.Rationale: Even though the rooster was frustrating him, Mr. Agbele helps the rooster when he gets hurt.

B.Choice: New skills should be shared with others.

C.Choice: It is better to live quietly than to be the center of attention.

D.Choice: True friendship means agreeing with each other at all times.

Content: Which quotation from the passage supports the answer in Part A?

A.Choice: “But when the rooster began trumpeting the time `text(hour)` after `text(hour)`, Mr. Agbele was distressed. . . . His life was being ruined by the rooster’s watch.” (paragraph `5`)

B.Choice: “‘The other roosters crow only at daybreak because they do not have watches. Since I have a watch, it is my duty to tell the time the rest of the `text(day)`.’” (paragraph `9`)

C.Choice: “The rooster clucked impatiently and said . . . ‘Perhaps you do not appreciate the service I perform, but I assure you that your neighbors do.’” (paragraph `13`)

D.Choice: “Gently Mr. Agbele took the rooster inside. He spent a `text(week)` feeding the poor bird corn broth and bathing his head with a cool towel until he was well again.” (paragraph `21`)

Key.Rationale: These lines show that Mr. Agbele cared for the rooster as the right thing to do, even though the rooster had been annoying him.
